ExampleSentence: Esta película me aburre mucho.
ExampleTranslation: This movie bores me a lot.
Notes: Works like "gustar": the thing that bores is the subject. "Me aburro" = I'm bored (reflexive).

ExampleSentence: ¿Te acuerdas de la fiesta del año pasado?
ExampleTranslation: Do you remember last year's party?
Notes: Reflexive, stem-changing o→ue. Always followed by "de."

ExampleSentence: Me acuesto a las once todas las noches.
ExampleTranslation: I go to bed at eleven every night.
Notes: Reflexive, stem-changing o→ue. Non-reflexive "acostar" = to put someone else to bed.

ExampleSentence: Mi papá se afeita todas las mañanas.
ExampleTranslation: My dad shaves every morning.
Notes: Reflexive. "La afeitadora" = razor/shaver.

ExampleSentence: La alarma sonó a las seis y no la escuché.
ExampleTranslation: The alarm went off at six and I didn't hear it.
Notes: Poner la alarma = to set the alarm.

ExampleSentence: ¿Quieres algo de comer?
ExampleTranslation: Do you want something to eat?
Notes: Opposite: "nada." Used in questions and affirmative sentences.

ExampleSentence: Alguien dejó la puerta abierta.
ExampleTranslation: Someone left the door open.
Notes: Opposite: "nadie." Takes singular verbs.

ExampleSentence: ¿Tienes alguna pregunta sobre la tarea?
ExampleTranslation: Do you have any questions about the homework?
Notes: Algún before masc. sing. nouns (algún día). Opposite: "ninguno/a."

ExampleSentence: Siempre desayuno antes de salir de casa.
ExampleTranslation: I always eat breakfast before leaving the house.
Notes: Antes de + infinitive. "Antes de que" + subjunctive. Opposite: "después (de)."

ExampleSentence: Hay una araña enorme en el baño.
ExampleTranslation: There's a huge spider in the bathroom.

ExampleSentence: Necesito tu ayuda con este proyecto.
ExampleTranslation: I need your help with this project.
Notes: Verb: "ayudar" (to help). "¡Ayuda!" = Help! (exclamation).

ExampleSentence: Los niños se bañan antes de cenar.
English: to bathe; to take a bath
ExampleTranslation: The kids bathe before dinner.
Notes: Reflexive. "La bañera" = bathtub.

Spanish: el baño, el cuarto de baño
ExampleSentence: ¿Dónde está el baño?
ExampleTranslation: Where is the bathroom?
Notes: El baño is everyday; "el cuarto de baño" is more formal.

ExampleSentence: Mi hija se cepilla el pelo después de ducharse.
ExampleTranslation: My daughter brushes her hair after showering.
Notes: Reflexive. Uses definite article "el pelo," not possessive.

ExampleSentence: Debes cepillarte los dientes tres veces al día.
ExampleTranslation: You should brush your teeth three times a day.
Notes: Reflexive. Uses "los dientes," not possessive.

ExampleSentence: ¿Dónde dejé mi cepillo?
ExampleTranslation: Where did I leave my brush?
Notes: El cepillo de dientes = toothbrush. "El cepillo de pelo" = hairbrush.

ExampleSentence: Se me acabó el champú. Necesito comprar más.
ExampleTranslation: I ran out of shampoo. I need to buy more.
Notes: Plural: los champús.

ExampleSentence: Compré una nueva crema de afeitar para mi esposo.
ExampleTranslation: I bought a new shaving cream for my husband.

ExampleSentence: Te llamaré cuando llegue a casa.
ExampleTranslation: I'll call you when I get home.
Notes: With future actions, it triggers subjunctive: "cuando llegue." For questions, use "¿cuándo?" with accent.

ExampleSentence: Estudio español desde hace dos años.
ExampleTranslation: I've been studying Spanish for two years.
Notes: Used with present tense for ongoing actions that started in the past.

ExampleSentence: ¡Qué desorden hay en tu habitación!
ExampleTranslation: What a mess there is in your room!
Notes: Opposite: "el orden" (order).

ExampleSentence: Mi despertador no sonó esta mañana.
ExampleTranslation: My alarm clock didn't go off this morning.
Notes: From the verb "despertar" (to wake).

ExampleSentence: Me despierto a las siete de la mañana.
ExampleTranslation: I wake up at seven in the morning.
Notes: Reflexive, stem-changing e→ie.

ExampleSentence: Primero desayuné y después fui al trabajo.
ExampleTranslation: First I had breakfast and then I went to work.
Notes: Stands alone (no "de"). Also: "luego," "entonces."

ExampleSentence: Después de cenar, vemos una película.
ExampleTranslation: After having dinner, we watch a movie.
Notes: Después de + infinitive or noun. Opposite: "antes (de)."

ExampleSentence: Me duermo fácilmente cuando estoy cansado.
English: to go to sleep; to fall asleep
ExampleTranslation: I fall asleep easily when I'm tired.
Notes: Reflexive, stem-changing o→ue. Non-reflexive "dormir" = to sleep.

ExampleSentence: La ducha del hotel tiene muy buena presión.
ExampleTranslation: The hotel shower has very good pressure.

ExampleSentence: Me ducho todas las mañanas antes de trabajar.
English: to shower; to take a shower
ExampleTranslation: I shower every morning before work.
Notes: Reflexive. Regular -ar verb.

ExampleSentence: Trabajé durante toda la noche.
ExampleTranslation: I worked during the whole night.
Notes: Also means "for" when describing duration.

ExampleSentence: —Gané la lotería. —¿En serio?
ExampleTranslation: I won the lottery. "Really?"
Notes: Expresses surprise or disbelief. Also: "¿De verdad?"

ExampleSentence: Me encanta la música clásica.
English: to like very much; to love (inanimate objects)
ExampleTranslation: I love classical music.
Notes: Works like "gustar": the thing loved is the subject. Don't use "amar" for objects/activities.

ExampleSentence: Mi jefe se enojó conmigo por llegar tarde.
ExampleTranslation: My boss got angry with me for being late.
Notes: Reflexive. In Spain: "enfadarse."

ExampleSentence: No tenía dinero; entonces no fui al cine.
ExampleTranslation: I didn't have money; then I didn't go to the movies.
Notes: Often means "so" or "in that case." Synonym: "luego."

ExampleSentence: Me miré en el espejo antes de salir.
ExampleTranslation: I looked at myself in the mirror before leaving.

ExampleSentence: Me faltan dos páginas para terminar el libro.
ExampleTranslation: I have two pages left to finish the book.
Notes: Works like "gustar." Literally "X is lacking to me."

ExampleSentence: Nos fascinan los documentales de naturaleza.
English: to fascinate; to like very much
ExampleTranslation: Nature documentaries fascinate us.
Notes: Works like "gustar." Stronger than "encantar."

ExampleSentence: Mi abuelo es muy gracioso; siempre nos hace reír.
ExampleTranslation: My grandpa is very funny; he always makes us laugh.
Notes: Changes for gender: gracioso/graciosa. "Divertido/a" also means fun/funny.

ExampleSentence: No grites, te puedo oír perfectamente.
ExampleTranslation: Don't shout, I can hear you perfectly.
Notes: Regular -ar verb.

ExampleSentence: No me importa lo que digan los demás.
English: to be important to; to matter
ExampleTranslation: I don't care what others say.
Notes: Works like "gustar." "No me importa" = I don't care / it doesn't matter to me.

ExampleSentence: El inodoro está tapado; llama al plomero.
ExampleTranslation: The toilet is clogged; call the plumber.
Notes: Also: "el retrete," "el váter" (Spain).

ExampleSentence: Me interesa mucho la historia antigua.
English: to be interesting to; to interest
ExampleTranslation: Ancient history really interests me.
Notes: Works like "gustar."

ExampleSentence: Ya es tarde; me voy.
ExampleTranslation: It's late now; I'm leaving.
Notes: Reflexive form of "ir." Emphasizes departure, not destination.

ExampleSentence: Lávate las manos con jabón.
ExampleTranslation: Wash your hands with soap.
Notes: Plural: los jabones.

ExampleSentence: Jamás volveré a ese restaurante.
ExampleTranslation: I will never go back to that restaurant.
Notes: Stronger/more emphatic than "nunca." "Nunca jamás" = never ever.

ExampleSentence: El lavabo del baño está roto.
ExampleTranslation: The bathroom sink is broken.
Notes: In some regions: "el lavamanos" or "el lavatorio."

ExampleSentence: Me lavo la cara con agua fría para despertarme.
ExampleTranslation: I wash my face with cold water to wake up.
Notes: Reflexive. "La cara," not "mi cara."

ExampleSentence: Lávate las manos antes de comer.
ExampleTranslation: Wash your hands before eating.
Notes: Reflexive. "Las manos," not "tus manos."

ExampleSentence: Me levanto temprano los fines de semana.
ExampleTranslation: I get up early on weekends.
Notes: Reflexive. Non-reflexive "levantar" = to lift.

ExampleSentence: Llámame cuando llegues a casa.
ExampleTranslation: Call me when you get home.
Notes: Regular -ar verb. "Llamar por teléfono" = to call on the phone.

ExampleSentence: ¿Cómo te llamas? Me llamo Ana.
English: to be called; to be named
ExampleTranslation: What's your name? My name is Ana.
Notes: Reflexive form of "llamar." Literally "to call oneself."

ExampleSentence: Primero estudio y luego salgo con amigos.
ExampleTranslation: First I study and then I go out with friends.
Notes: Also: "¡Hasta luego!" = See you later!

ExampleSentence: Ella lleva muy poco maquillaje.
ExampleTranslation: She wears very little makeup.

ExampleSentence: Mi hermana se maquilla antes de salir.
ExampleTranslation: My sister puts on makeup before going out.
Notes: Reflexive.

ExampleSentence: Te veo más tarde en el café.
ExampleTranslation: I'll see you later at the café.

ExampleSentence: Me molesta el ruido de la calle.
ExampleTranslation: The street noise bothers me.
Notes: Works like "gustar." False friend — does not mean "to molest."

ExampleSentence: No hay nada en el refrigerador.
ExampleTranslation: There's nothing in the fridge.
Notes: Opposite: "algo." With double negative: "No... nada."

ExampleSentence: Nadie me llamó ayer.
ExampleTranslation: No one called me yesterday.
Notes: Opposite: "alguien." With double negative: "No... nadie."

ExampleSentence: Ni mi hermano ni yo sabemos cocinar.
ExampleTranslation: Neither my brother nor I know how to cook.
Notes: Opposite: "o... o."

ExampleSentence: No tengo ningún plan para el sábado.
ExampleTranslation: I have no plans for Saturday.
Notes: Ningún before masc. sing. nouns. Almost always singular. Opposite: "alguno/a."

ExampleSentence: Nunca he estado en Argentina.
ExampleTranslation: I have never been to Argentina.
Notes: With double negative: "No... nunca." Similar to "jamás."

ExampleSentence: O vienes conmigo o te quedas en casa.
ExampleTranslation: Either you come with me or you stay home.
Notes: Opposite: "ni... ni."

ExampleSentence: En casa siempre llevo pantuflas.
ExampleTranslation: At home I always wear slippers.
Notes: Also: "las zapatillas" in some regions.

ExampleSentence: Se me acabó la pasta de dientes.
ExampleTranslation: I ran out of toothpaste.
Notes: Also: "la pasta dental," "la crema dental."

ExampleSentence: Ella se peina el cabello antes de salir.
ExampleTranslation: She combs her hair before going out.
Notes: Reflexive. "El peine" = the comb.

ExampleSentence: Me pongo el abrigo porque hace frío.
ExampleTranslation: I put on my coat because it's cold.
Notes: Reflexive of "poner" (irregular: yo pongo). Used for clothing. Opposite: "quitarse."

ExampleSentence: Mi mamá se puso triste con la noticia.
ExampleTranslation: My mom became sad with the news.
Notes: Used with adjectives to describe a change of state or mood.

ExampleSentence: Estaba enfermo; por eso no fui a la fiesta.
ExampleTranslation: I was sick; that's why I didn't go to the party.

ExampleSentence: Siempre corro por la mañana.
ExampleTranslation: I always run in the morning.
Notes: Use "de la mañana" with a specific time: "a las 8 de la mañana."

ExampleSentence: Preferimos cenar por la noche.
ExampleTranslation: We prefer to have dinner at night.
Notes: Use "de la noche" with a specific time: "a las 10 de la noche."

ExampleSentence: Voy al gimnasio por la tarde.
English: in the afternoon; in the evening
ExampleTranslation: I go to the gym in the afternoon.
Notes: Use "de la tarde" with a specific time.

ExampleSentence: Por último, quiero agradecerles a todos.
ExampleTranslation: Finally, I want to thank you all.
Notes: Used to introduce the last item in a sequence. Also: "finalmente."

ExampleSentence: No te preocupes por mí; estoy bien.
ExampleTranslation: Don't worry about me; I'm fine.
Notes: Reflexive. Followed by "por."

ExampleSentence: Me voy a probar estos zapatos.
ExampleTranslation: I'm going to try on these shoes.
Notes: Reflexive, stem-changing o→ue. Non-reflexive "probar" = to try/taste.

ExampleSentence: Me quedan dos dólares en la billetera.
English: to be left over; to fit (clothing)
ExampleTranslation: I have two dollars left in my wallet.
Notes: Works like "gustar." Also: "Este vestido te queda bien" = This dress fits you well.

ExampleSentence: Me quedé en casa todo el fin de semana.
ExampleTranslation: I stayed home all weekend.
Notes: Reflexive. Different meaning from "quedar."

ExampleSentence: Quítate los zapatos antes de entrar.
ExampleTranslation: Take off your shoes before entering.
Notes: Reflexive. Used for clothing. Opposite: "ponerse."

ExampleSentence: Mi rutina diaria comienza a las seis de la mañana.
ExampleTranslation: My daily routine starts at six in the morning.

ExampleSentence: Me seco el pelo con una toalla.
ExampleTranslation: I dry my hair with a towel.
Notes: Reflexive. Spelling change in preterite: yo me sequé.

ExampleSentence: Por favor, siéntate aquí.
ExampleTranslation: Please, sit down here.
Notes: Reflexive, stem-changing e→ie.

ExampleSentence: Me siento muy feliz hoy.
ExampleTranslation: I feel very happy today.
Notes: Reflexive, stem-changing e→ie. For emotions/states: "Me siento triste/cansado."

ExampleSentence: Siento un dolor en la espalda.
ExampleTranslation: I feel a pain in my back.
Notes: Non-reflexive, stem-changing e→ie. For sensations or regret: "Lo siento" = I'm sorry.

ExampleSentence: Siempre llego temprano al trabajo.
ExampleTranslation: I always arrive early to work.
Notes: Opposite: "nunca."

ExampleSentence: A mí también me gusta el chocolate.
ExampleTranslation: I like chocolate too.
Notes: Opposite: "tampoco."

ExampleSentence: A mí tampoco me gusta el café.
ExampleTranslation: I don't like coffee either.
Notes: Used in negative sentences. Opposite: "también."

ExampleSentence: Necesito una toalla limpia para la ducha.
ExampleTranslation: I need a clean towel for the shower.

ExampleSentence: Me visto rápido porque voy tarde.
ExampleTranslation: I get dressed quickly because I'm running late.
Notes: Reflexive, stem-changing e→i. Non-reflexive "vestir" = to dress (someone).
